card: Enables SQLite secure_delete by default when opening wallet databases and in the SQLite depends package, ensuring deleted or overwritten data is zeroed out on disk. Rotating a wallet passphrase previously left superseded master key records lingering in SQLite database free space, because explicit purging via VACUUM only occurred on initial encryption. The change eliminates WalletDatabase::Rewrite and adds functional tests verifying that unencrypted keys and rotated master keys do not remain in the raw database file.
changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the patch or approach.
evidence: PR description: "l0rinc's LLMs recently found changing the passphrase can leave the original that encryption key record in free pages. We should want to ensure that those records are also deleted... Note that this behavior appears to be present since wallet encryption was initially introduced in #352."

PR description: "[Debian], [Ubuntu], [Fedora], [Arch], and [NixOS] all set SQLite's compile time option to default secure_delete to enabled... As I run Arch and often do not use depends builds, I had not noticed that secure_delete was always on and did not experience any particularly poor wallet performance that could be attributed to that behavior."
problem: Sensitive wallet records can persist in unallocated SQLite database pages after deletions or updates. While initial wallet encryption previously called VACUUM to purge unencrypted private keys, other updates such as passphrase changes (which rotate the master encryption key) left superseded key records intact in database free space.

risk.why: A bug in database connection setup or disk writes could corrupt wallet files or cause unexpected performance degradation during wallet operations.

summary: Enables SQLite's secure_delete PRAGMA by default when opening wallet databases and sets -DSQLITE_SECURE_DELETE in the SQLite depends build. This causes SQLite to overwrite deleted or modified records with zeroes rather than leaving them in free pages. The change removes WalletDatabase::Rewrite, which previously ran an explicit VACUUM only during initial wallet encryption, and adds functional test coverage verifying key erasure.
